appdata.name: AppData Scanner
appdata.help: Searches the Roaming and Local AppData folders for files and folders whose names match known cheat keywords. Many cheat loaders unpack their files or store configs here.

prefetch.name: Prefetch Scanner
prefetch.help: Reads C:\Windows\Prefetch, where Windows records every program launch. Reveals cheats that were executed in the past — even if the files were deleted afterwards.

recentfiles.name: Recent Files Scanner
recentfiles.help: Checks the Windows recent-files list for documents and executables the user opened recently, including files that have since been removed.

gamefolder.name: Game Folder Scanner
gamefolder.help: Inspects the game installation folder for foreign files: injected DLLs, modified configs, or leftover cheat files.

registry.name: Registry Scanner
registry.desc: Registry search by keywords (MuiCache, AppSwitched, ShowJumpView)
registry.help: Searches forensic registry keys (MuiCache, AppSwitched, ShowJumpView) where Windows logs the names of programs that ran. These traces survive file deletion.

browserhistory.name: Browser History Scanner
browserhistory.desc: Deep search of browser history and caches by keywords
browserhistory.help: Deep-searches the history and caches of installed browsers for visits to cheat sites, downloads, and related keywords.

process.name: Process Scanner
process.desc: Scanning running processes with paths and command lines
process.help: Lists all running processes with their full paths and command lines and matches them against cheat keywords — catches software that is active right now.

steam.name: Steam Scanner
steam.help: Examines Steam on this PC: which accounts have logged in, and whether suspicious files are present inside the Steam directory.

amcache.name: Amcache Scanner
amcache.desc: Scanning Amcache for program execution history
amcache.help: Parses the Amcache hive, where Windows keeps a record of executed programs with paths and timestamps — even for files that no longer exist.

bam.name: BAM/DAM Scanner
bam.desc: Scanning Background Activity Moderator for execution history
bam.help: Reads the Background Activity Moderator (BAM/DAM), a Windows service that tracks which programs each user ran recently.

shellbags.name: Shellbags Scanner
shellbags.desc: Scanning Shellbags for folder access history
shellbags.help: Analyzes ShellBag registry data, which records every folder ever opened in Explorer — exposes cheat folders even after they were deleted.

vm.name: VM Scanner
vm.desc: Detection of virtual machines and sandbox environments
vm.help: Detects whether Custos is running inside a virtual machine or sandbox — a common trick to present a clean PC during a screen check.

dnscache.name: DNS Cache Scanner
dnscache.desc: Scanning Windows DNS cache for suspicious domain resolutions
dnscache.help: Inspects the Windows DNS cache for recently resolved cheat-related domains — shows which sites this PC contacted since the last reboot.

scheduledtasks.name: Scheduled Tasks Scanner
scheduledtasks.desc: Scanning Windows Task Scheduler for suspicious persistence entries
scheduledtasks.help: Scans the Windows Task Scheduler for suspicious entries that relaunch cheat software or keep it persistent across reboots.

filehash.name: File Hash Scanner
filehash.desc: SHA-256 hashing of Downloads/Desktop/Temp against known cheat hashes
filehash.help: Computes SHA-256 hashes of files in Downloads, Desktop and Temp and compares them against a database of known cheat hashes — catches renamed files.

windowmodule.name: Window & Module Scanner
windowmodule.desc: Scans process window titles and loaded modules against the keyword list
windowmodule.help: Matches the window titles and loaded modules of running processes against the keyword list — finds cheats hiding behind renamed executables.

antiforensics.name: Anti-Forensics Scanner
antiforensics.desc: Detecting cleared logs, wiped Prefetch, trace cleaners and blocked Windows tools
antiforensics.help: Looks for signs that traces were removed before the check — Prefetch disabled or wiped, event logs cleared recently, trace cleaners (CCleaner, PrivaZer, BleachBit, SDelete, USB Oblivion…) run in the last few days — and for Windows components switched off so checks or checking tools cannot run: tools blocked via Image File Execution Options or DisallowRun (Task Manager, Registry Editor, Process Explorer, Everything, Custos…), Task Manager / Registry Editor / Command Prompt disabled by policy, the Event Log, BAM or DNS Client service disabled, or reg.exe itself blocked. Only these specific signs are reported, and legitimate setups (Process Explorer replacing Task Manager, parental DisallowRun lists for games) are ignored. Not proof of cheating on its own — but it explains why other scanners may come back empty.

manual-shortcuts.name: Folder & settings shortcuts
manual-shortcuts.desc: Open Windows folders and settings pages
manual-shortcuts.help: One-click shortcuts to the Windows folders and settings pages most commonly checked during a manual review.

manual-registry.name: Registry shortcuts
manual-registry.desc: Jump to forensic registry keys in regedit
manual-registry.help: Opens regedit directly at forensic registry keys so you can inspect program-execution traces yourself.

manual-links.name: Reference links
manual-links.desc: Open Telegram and marketplace reference links
manual-links.help: Quick links to Telegram bots and marketplaces where cheats are sold — useful for checking whether the user has interacted with them.

tool-lastactivityview.name: LastActivityView
tool-lastactivityview.help: NirSoft tool that builds a timeline of computer activity: program launches, opened files, and system events.

tool-usbdeview.name: USBDeview
tool-usbdeview.help: NirSoft tool that lists every USB device ever connected to this PC — helps spot flash drives used to carry cheats.

tool-everything.name: Everything
tool-everything.help: Instant file-name search across all NTFS drives — far faster and more complete than Windows search.

tool-systeminformer.name: System Informer
tool-systeminformer.help: Advanced process viewer (formerly Process Hacker): inspect threads, loaded modules, handles and memory of running processes.

tool-shellbaganalyzer.name: ShellBag Analyzer
tool-shellbaganalyzer.help: Inspects and cleans ShellBag data — the folder-browsing traces Explorer leaves in the registry.

export-csv.name: CSV export
export-csv.help: Saves all scan findings to a text file for sharing or archiving.

export-json.name: JSON export
export-json.help: Saves the full scan report as machine-readable JSON.

defender.name: Defender History Scanner
defender.desc: Windows Defender detections of cheats and cheat tools
defender.help: Reads Windows Defender's own detection history. When Defender caught a game cheat or cheat tool (e.g. HackTool:Win64/GameHack, CheatEngine), the record — threat name, file path, time, action — remains even after the file was deleted or quarantined. Windows activators and keygens that Defender also labels HackTool are ignored unless their file is named like a known cheat. A Defender cheat identification raises the verdict to at least High.

recyclebin.name: Recycle Bin Scanner
recyclebin.desc: Deleted files in the Recycle Bin matched against cheat names
recyclebin.help: Reads the Recycle Bin metadata of every drive: for each deleted item, its original path and the exact time it was deleted. Items named like a known cheat are reported, with a note when the file can still be restored.

usb.name: USB History Scanner
usb.desc: USB storage devices ever connected, with first and last connection times
usb.help: Lists every USB storage device ever connected (from the registry), with when it was first installed (setupapi.dev.log) and last connected (partition events). Shown as system information in the timeline — a flash drive plugged in minutes before the check, next to a program that ran from that drive, is worth a question.

usnjournal.name: USN Journal Scanner
usnjournal.desc: NTFS change journal: created, renamed and deleted cheat files
usnjournal.help: Reads the NTFS change journal of the system drive, which records every file created, renamed, written and deleted. Any file that ever carried a cheat-like name is reported with its full rename chain (e.g. aimbot.dll → update.dll) and when it was last touched — even if it was deleted long ago. Requires administrator rights; very large journals are read for up to ~20 seconds.

aob.name: AOB Memory Signature Scan
aob.help: Scans the game process memory for byte signatures (AOB patterns) of known cheats.

injected-module.name: Injected Module / Manual-Map Scan
injected-module.help: Looks for DLLs injected into the game: denylisted names, modules without an on-disk path (manual mapping), suspicious load paths, and private executable memory regions.

mono.name: Mono Debugger-Agent Check
mono.help: Checks whether the Mono runtime was started with a debugger agent or loaded from an unusual path — a common pattern for Unturned cheat loaders.

thread-start.name: Thread Start-Address Check
thread-start.help: Verifies that every thread in the game starts inside a legitimately loaded module; threads starting in raw memory indicate injected code.

self-integrity.name: Self-Integrity Check
self-integrity.help: Makes sure Custos itself is not being debugged or tampered with during the scan.

hook.name: IAT / Inline Hook Check
hook.help: Reads the prologues of hook-prone WinAPI exports inside the game process to spot inline hooks and trampolines installed by cheats.

orchestrator.name: Live Scan
orchestrator.help: Status messages from the live-scan engine.

hookSkippedArch.title: Hook check skipped
hookSkippedArch.detail: Inline-hook detection uses x64 instruction patterns and is skipped on {{arch}} builds to avoid false positives.

hookSkippedModules.title: Hook check skipped
hookSkippedModules.detail: Could not enumerate the target process modules, so export addresses could not be validated against it. Skipped to avoid false positives.

moduleNoPath.title: Suspicious module detected
moduleNoPath.detail: Module "{{module}}" has no on-disk path (possible manual map)

privateExecRwx.title: Private executable memory region
privateExecRwx.detail: MEM_PRIVATE + executable protection at {{address}} (size: {{size}} bytes) — writable+executable, possible manual-mapped code

privateExecJit.title: Private executable memory region
privateExecJit.detail: MEM_PRIVATE + executable protection at {{address}} (size: {{size}} bytes) — executable private page (may be JIT/Mono)

monoDebuggerAgent.title: Mono soft-debugger agent enabled
monoDebuggerAgent.detail: The game was launched with --debugger-agent=, which lets a managed debugger attach. Common when developing/loading cheats.

threadOutsideModule.title: Thread starting outside any module
threadOutsideModule.detail: A thread starts at {{address}}, which is not inside any loaded module — possible injected/manual-mapped code.

debuggerPresent.title: Debugger detected (IsDebuggerPresent)
debuggerPresent.detail: A debugger is attached to the Custos process. This may indicate an attempt to analyse or tamper with the scanner.

remoteDebugger.title: Remote debugger detected (CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent)
remoteDebugger.detail: CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent returned true for the Custos process. A kernel-level or cross-process debugger may be attached.

nativeUnavailableArm64.title: Native module unavailable ({{arch}} build)
nativeUnavailableArm64.detail: The Win32 bridge Live Scan uses (koffi) did not load in this {{arch}} build. If this persists, run the x64 build (custos-x64.exe) on Windows 11 ARM, where it works under emulation.

nativeUnavailableX64.title: Native module unavailable ({{arch}} build)
nativeUnavailableX64.detail: The Win32 bridge Live Scan uses (koffi) did not load in this {{arch}} build. Try re-downloading the latest release.

nativeUnavailableNonWin.title: Native module unavailable (Windows only)
nativeUnavailableNonWin.detail: Live memory scanning uses Windows APIs and only works on Windows. Run Custos on a Windows machine to use this feature.

gameNotRunning.title: Game not running — start it and rescan
gameNotRunning.detail: The live scanner could not find a running game process. Launch your game and click "Live Scan" again.

openProcessFailed.title: Failed to open game process
openProcessFailed.detail: Could not open a handle to {{name}} (PID {{pid}}). Ensure Custos is running as Administrator.

processChanged.title: Process changed during scan
processChanged.detail: The process at PID {{pid}} is now "{{opened}}", not "{{expected}}". Aborting to avoid scanning the wrong process.

help.scanPage: Runs all forensic scanners against this PC: file system, registry, execution history (Prefetch, Amcache, BAM), processes, Steam, DNS cache and more. Results appear on the Results tab.
help.liveScanPage: Attaches to the running game process and scans its memory in real time: cheat signatures, injected modules, suspicious threads and hooks. Run it while the game is open.

manual.systemTools: Opens Windows settings pages for a quick manual look — for example, Data Usage shows which apps used the network recently.
manual.folders: Folders where cheats are typically stored or leave traces. Look for recently changed files and suspicious executables.
manual.games: Game and Steam installation folders — check for foreign DLLs and recently modified files.
manual.registry: Forensic registry keys where Windows logs program execution. Each button opens regedit at the exact key.
manual.telegram: Cheats are often sold through these Telegram bots. Opening a bot in the user's Telegram can reveal whether they have interacted with it.
manual.resources: Marketplaces where cheats are commonly sold. Review purchase history together with the user if needed.

verdict.title: Risk verdict
verdict.leadsNotProof: Findings are leads, not proof — investigate before acting.
verdict.keyEvidenceHint: The same signature was found by several independent checks — the strongest kind of lead.

reason.no-findings: Nothing matched any known cheat signature.
reason.verified-hash: A file matches the hash of a known cheat build.
reason.strong-corroboration: A cheat signature was confirmed by 3+ independent artifact types.
reason.corroboration: A cheat signature was confirmed by several independent artifacts.
reason.community-hash-uncorroborated: An unverified (community) hash matched but nothing else confirms it.
reason.multiple-leads: Several independent leads, none confirmed by another artifact.
reason.lone-match: An isolated name match — likely a coincidence until something confirms it.
reason.environment-only: Only information about the system, no cheat evidence.
reason.incomplete-coverage: {{failed}} of {{total}} checks did not complete — the picture is incomplete. Run Custos as Administrator and scan again.
reason.trace-cleaning: Signs that traces were removed or Windows components were switched off before the check (cleared logs, wiped Prefetch, a cleaner run, blocked checking tools) — other results may be incomplete.
reason.trace-cleaning-with-leads: Traces were cleaned or checking tools blocked, AND cheat leads remain — a combination that warrants a close look.
reason.defender-cheat: Windows Defender itself identified a game cheat or cheat tool on this PC.

report.title: CUSTOS — FORENSIC SCAN REPORT
report.integrityNote: Any edit to the JSON export changes this hash — compare it to verify the report is unmodified.

timeline.title: Activity timeline
timeline.hint: Every lead that carries a time — last program runs, execution records, site visits, log clears — in order. Activity shortly before the check is highlighted.

triage.ignoreHint: Stop treating this signature as a lead on every future scan (e.g. a legitimate program on your server that shares the name).
triage.dismissedNote: Marked as a false positive — excluded from the verdict.
triage.ignoredSignature: Signature “{{signature}}” is ignored — excluded from the verdict.
triage.pathMissing: This file or folder no longer exists.
triage.ignoredHint: These signatures are skipped on every scan. Remove one to count it again.
